models_evaluated: persistent postoperative opioid use prediction model

links.outcome: Model AUC and other metrics in Black versus White patients, before and after subgroup matching
links.effect: Black patients (<5% of sample) showed substantially higher AUC than White patients; across both models the differences were attenuated after matching on patient characteristics.
links.quote: Across both models, performance differences - measured by AUC and other performance metrics - were attenuated after matching, suggesting that upstream biases may paradoxically inflate apparent model performance in minoritized patient groups.

unlisted_practices: Subgroup matching on patient covariates to interpret apparent subgroup performance differences in prediction models

screen.reason: The study empirically investigates subgroup performance disparity and tests subgroup-level covariate alignment/matching as an audit practice for evaluating equity in clinical predictive risk models.

primary.practice: subgroup covariate matching / fair metric evaluation
